description: Ocular-dominance critical period of primary visual cortex: opening when parvalbumin-cell inhibition matures, closing with perineuronal-net condensation; enzymatic removal of the nets reopens it. Ages for choosing the gate's schedule positions and thresholds; the stage itself takes only Params.
reopening: chondroitinase ABC degrades perineuronal nets and restores ocular-dominance plasticity in adults (Pizzorusso et al. 2002): critical_period_gate with reopen = true

windows[0].quantity: ages of eye opening, opening, peak and closing of the ocular-dominance critical period
windows[0].note: Abstracts plus the full text of the Espinosa & Stryker review. P19 was the youngest age tested in 1996, so the onset may be earlier; plasticity declines progressively to about P110. Eye opening P13-P14 rests on a secondary source that gives P12-P14.

windows[1].quantity: ages of opening, peak and closing of the ocular-dominance critical period
windows[1].note: The peak is a plateau from the 4th to the 6th-8th week rather than a point at week 6. Closing at about 3 months is the classic definition; plasticity of the extragranular layers persists to about 1 year (Daw et al. 1992).

gate_params_example.quantity: example parameters of the critical_period_gate stage
gate_params_example.note: Illustrative values (open threshold, closing delay) for the stage; not from a paper.

reopening.quantity: reopening of adult ocular-dominance plasticity by chondroitinase ABC
reopening.note: The mechanism cited for closing (perineuronal-net condensation) is correlational plus reactivation, not shown to be causal.
